risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: mech_docs WRITE was authorised by the licence key alone -- a key shipped to the browser and readable by anyone who can open sairnmechanical.html. It is the one of the four MECH_RECORDS tables whose own server-side redactor carries patterns for SSN, EIN and card-length digit runs, because scanDoc() asks a model to extract every field off work orders, contracts, permits and invoices and the answer is stored on the row. api/_lib/mech-redact.js reduces that text and never refuses a write, deliberately, so it was not the gate and there was no other one. Fixed as one registry entry in each of SD_SESSION_GATED and SD_GATE_APP.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnmechanical) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sairnmechanical.html claimed a capability it never invoked. The Technician Credentials panel subtitle read 'Licences, certifications and expiry -- the record dispatch eligibility is computed from', while every mechData() call in the file was read or write. api/_lib/mech-credentials.js evaluateEligibility, the eligibility action in api/sd-data.js, the registry entry in api/_resources/sairnmechanical.js and ten engine test arms all existed and nothing in the product reached them; the word eligibility appeared exactly once in the app, in that sentence. Not a security hole -- nothing was bypassed because nothing was called -- but a claim the product did not support. Fixed by wiring a dispatch-eligibility card that sends the action, renders the server verdict without recomputing any expiry, and distinguishes a refusal from an empty answer.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnmechanical) has this defect on record
risks.risk: mech_docs stored and SERVER-SYNCED raw AI-extracted document text verbatim, with no redaction of any kind. sairnmechanical.html's scanDoc() asks the model, in its own words, to 'EXTRACT: Every field -- names, dates, amounts, codes, reference numbers' from photographed work orders, maintenance contracts, permits, inspection reports and INVOICES; saveDoc() then stored el.textContent unchanged as {id,date,text} and mechPushRecord pushed it to the mech_docs table. A customer's name, site address and phone number reached a server because a technician photographed a work order. SECOND HALF: the toast said 'Saved on this device' ONE LINE AFTER the push, and the comment above the function still asserted 'there is no server data layer for this app yet' -- true when written, false since mech_docs was registered in api/_resources/sairnmechanical.js.

Four divergences, client wrong in all four: a suite number left beside the address token; a labelled phone giving Phone: 555-[ADDRESS REDACTED]: RTU-4 with the number half-leaked AND the equipment label destroyed; Qty 12 Unit: RTU-4 destroyed on a non-address; and a labelled seven-digit local number left intact. The parity arm that exists to catch exactly this saw only ONE of the four, because its case list had not grown when the rules did.
